summary: Iteration 15 image-compression backend tests: 7/7 PASSED. Validated (B) 4000x3000 JPEG resized to max-edge 1200 with ~90%+ byte reduction, (C) 2000x1500 RGBA PNG kept as PNG with alpha & resized to 1200, (D) 400x300 JPEG not upscaled and served at original dims, (E) 500 KB video/mp4 bytes untouched, (F) db.uploads row contains original_bytes/bytes/compression_ratio (<1.0), (G) regression: text/plain -> 400 and no-auth -> 401. All GET /api/files/... downloads decode correctly with PIL and preserve aspect ratio within 1 px.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py _compress_image: RGBA JPEGs from phones with EXIF alpha channel are correctly detected via img.mode; palette-with-transparency also handled ('P' + 'transparency'). Looks good.
Compression uses run_in_threadpool so it does not block the event loop -- appropriate for CPU-bound Pillow work.
Compression failures are swallowed (bare except) and original bytes are stored. Consider logging the exception (currently silent) so ops can spot systemic decode failures.
compression_ratio is stored rounded to 3 decimals; harmless but note downstream analytics should treat it as approximate.
server.py is 1832 lines -- above the 700 line guideline in the review rubric; consider splitting media/upload, merchant, deals, and auth into separate routers for maintainability.
seed_data_creation: One OTP-registered user (+911234567915, 'IT15 Frank') and 5 uploads in db.uploads (large jpeg x2, rgba png, small jpeg, mp4). No production/seed data modified.
